name: saxes
input_api: new SaxesParser({xmlns: true}); on('opentag'|'closetag'|'text'|'cdata'|'comment'|'processinginstruction'|'error'); write(string).close() after strict UTF-8 TextDecoder of local bytes
scope: One namespace-aware XML 1.0 document from local bytes as a SAX event stream with resolved element and attribute namespace URIs
family: saxes hand-written XML 1.0 + Namespaces state machine (sax-js fork)
family_note: saxes.js implements its own character-by-character state machine (sText, sOpenTag, sAttrib, sCData, sPI, sEntity, ...), entity decoding, and xmlns prefix binding with well-formedness checks; xmlchars 2.2.0 supplies only XML 1.0/1.1 and Namespaces character-class regexes. It does not wrap expat, libxml2, or a DOMParser. It originated as a fork of sax-js but its parser code was rewritten and is maintained separately, so sax is logged as a distinct lead.

name: jsdom
input_api: new JSDOM(text, {contentType: 'application/xml', virtualConsole}) on local bytes decoded with strict UTF-8 TextDecoder; jsdom's XML document parser runs new SaxesParser({xmlns: true, defaultXMLVersion: '1.0', forceXMLVersion: true}), throws a SyntaxError on the first saxes error, and builds the DOM; the adapter treats any jsdomError as fatal and reads window.document: element and attribute namespaceURI/localName, attribute order, and Text/CDATASection data in document order
scope: One namespace-aware XML 1.0 document from locally decoded text as a jsdom XML Document with saxes-resolved element and attribute namespace URIs; comments and processing instructions are kept as DOM nodes
family: saxes XML 1.0 + Namespaces state machine (saxes 6.0.0) under jsdom's XML document builder
family_note: jsdom 31.0.1 has no XML tokenizer of its own: lib/jsdom/browser/parser/xml.js creates SaxesParser({xmlns: true, defaultXMLVersion: '1.0', forceXMLVersion: true}) and maps its opentag, closetag, text, cdata, comment, processinginstruction and doctype events to DOM nodes; HTML goes through parse5 instead. The package.json range saxes ^6.0.0 resolves to saxes 6.0.0, the same release and npm integrity as the selected saxes path, so the two paths share one parser family and one tokenizer source; jsdom is a separate API path with its own DOM construction. jsdom adds one extension of its own: entity declarations matching <!ENTITY name "value"> in the DOCTYPE text are copied into saxes' entity table. It forces XML 1.0 rules even for documents declaring version 1.1, and drops text outside the root element. DOMParser.parseFromString(text, 'application/xml') uses the same parseIntoDocument path but reports errors as a parsererror document rather than throwing; the adapter uses the JSDOM constructor.
verification_note: jsdom is an API path over the selected saxes 6.0.0 tokenizer, not a separate parser engine; the receipt counts jsdom package lines, jsdom's own XML document parser lib/jsdom/browser/parser/xml.js alone, and saxes saxes.js lines separately. The jsdom package count is dominated by module loading and window setup; the coverage run only constructs the document and closes the window, so the adapter's DOM read-back is not counted. Both valid controls, catalog-ns.xml and order-default-ns.xml, match the expat oracle exactly, including namespace URIs, attribute order and text; comments and processing instructions remain DOM nodes and split text as in expat. AFL++ feedback spans /work/node_modules/ during construction only: saxes, jsdom XML tree construction and DOM node creation, plus input-independent module-load and window setup ranges; window named-property and id-cache updates from id attributes are input-dependent jsdom construction, and xmlchars ranges are saxes character-class checks. Scope limits: jsdom copies DOCTYPE <!ENTITY name "value"> declarations into saxes' entity table (a jsdom extension, not general DTD processing), forces XML 1.0 rules for version 1.1 documents, and drops text outside the root element. DOMParser.parseFromString shares parseIntoDocument but turns errors into a parsererror document; it was not the measured path. No malformed-input, resource-use, or fuzz campaign was run.

name: sax
input_api: sax.parser(true, {xmlns: true, strictEntities: true}).write(string).close() after strict UTF-8 TextDecoder of local bytes; documented createStream(true, {xmlns: true}) also accepts a local file stream
scope: One namespace-aware XML 1.0 document from local bytes as SAX events with expanded element/attribute names
family: sax-js hand-written strict XML state machine
family_note: sax 1.6.1 parses through lib/sax.js with its own strict SAX tokenizer, entity handling, CDATA and xmlns bindings. Saxes forked sax-js but rewrote and maintains a distinct parser implementation; the two package paths share historical lineage, not parser code.

name: fast-xml-parser
input_api: new XMLParser({preserveOrder: true, ignoreAttributes: false, commentPropName: '#comment', trimValues: false, parseTagValue: false, htmlEntities: true}).parse(Buffer, true) on local bytes; the package decodes the Buffer with Buffer#toString and runs its own XMLValidator first. fast-xml-parser does no namespace processing, so the adapter resolves element and attribute prefixes from in-scope xmlns attributes and rejects unbound prefixes and duplicate expanded attributes
scope: One XML 1.0 document from local bytes as an order-preserving JS object tree with qualified names; namespace URIs are resolved by the adapter, not by the package
family_note: src/xmlparser/OrderedObjParser.js scans the decoded string for tags, attributes (one regex per tag), CDATA, comments, PIs and DOCTYPE, and src/validator.js is a separate well-formedness scan run by parse(data, true). Entity and numeric character reference decoding is delegated to @nodable/entities 3.1.0 (same author group); numeric references are decoded only with the documented htmlEntities option, which also admits common HTML named entities. It does not wrap expat, libxml2, sax, saxes, or a DOMParser. The package has no namespace URI resolution (only removeNSPrefix), so the expanded names in the result come from the adapter's Namespaces in XML 1.0 prefix resolution over the parser's qualified names and xmlns attributes, as in the pugixml path.

name: @xmldom/xmldom
input_api: new DOMParser({onError}).parseFromString(text, 'application/xml') on in-memory text from a strict UTF-8 TextDecoder of local bytes; the adapter's onError throws on every warning, error or fatalError; the summary reads the returned Document's namespaceURI/localName/attributes
input_note: parseFromString accepts only a string for XML MIME types, so the adapter decodes the local bytes; under the general protocol's local in-memory text rule the package itself parses all markup structure.
scope: One namespace-aware XML 1.0 document from locally decoded text as a W3C DOM Level 2 Core Document with resolved element and attribute namespace URIs
family: xmldom XMLReader tokenizer + DOMHandler DOM builder (jindw/xmldom lineage)
family_note: @xmldom/xmldom 0.9.12 has no runtime dependencies. lib/sax.js holds its own XMLReader (a hand-written indexOf/regex tag scanner with namespace prefix scoping and entity decoding via lib/entities.js and lib/grammar.js); lib/dom-parser.js feeds those events to DOMHandler, which builds lib/dom.js nodes. It does not import sax-js, saxes, expat, or libxml2; its lib/sax.js is unrelated to the sax npm package despite the file name. The deprecated unscoped xmldom 0.6.0 is the predecessor of this family. Lenient by default: without onError, warnings and recoverable errors are logged and parsing continues, so the adapter makes every report fatal.

name: xml2js
input_api: new xml2js.Parser({xmlns: true, explicitChildren: true, preserveChildrenOrder: true, charsAsChildren: true, includeWhiteChars: true, charkey: '#text'}).parseStringPromise(text) on local bytes decoded with strict UTF-8 TextDecoder; xml2js runs sax.parser(strict=true, {xmlns: true}) and the adapter reads the resulting object tree: $ns element URIs and local names, sax attribute objects under $, and document-ordered element and text children under $$
scope: One namespace-aware XML 1.0 document from local bytes as an xml2js object tree with sax-resolved element and attribute namespace URIs and ordered children; comments and processing instructions are dropped, so text split only by them is reported as one run
family: sax-js strict XML state machine (sax 1.6.1) under the xml2js object builder
family_note: xml2js 0.6.2 has no tokenizer of its own: lib/parser.js creates sax.parser(strict, {trim: false, normalize: false, xmlns}) and builds objects from its opentag, closetag, text and cdata events. The package.json range sax >=0.6.0 resolves to sax 1.6.1, the same release as the selected sax path, so the two paths share one parser family and one tokenizer source; xml2js is a separate API path with its own object mapping. xml2js does not pass strictEntities, so sax uses its HTML-extended entity table rather than only the five XML predefined entities. xml2js ignores comment, processing-instruction and DOCTYPE events. xmlbuilder 11.0.1 is loaded only for xml2js.Builder and is not on the parse path.
verification_note: xml2js is an API path over the selected sax 1.6.1 tokenizer, not a separate parser engine; the receipt counts xml2js package lines and sax lib/sax.js lines separately, and AFL++ feedback spans both. Both valid controls, catalog-ns.xml and order-default-ns.xml, match the expat oracle exactly, including namespace URIs, attribute order and text. Scope limits: xml2js drops comment and processing-instruction events, so a text run split only by a comment or PI is reported as one segment where expat reports two (both controls place them beside whitespace only); xml2js does not pass sax strictEntities, so sax's HTML-extended entity table is accepted; DOCTYPE events are ignored. The adapter sets the documented charkey option to '#text' because the default '_' is a legal element name. No malformed-input, resource-use, or fuzz campaign was run.

name: xml-js
input_api: xmljs.xml2js(text, {compact:false, captureSpacesBetweenElements:true, alwaysChildren:true}) on strictly UTF-8 decoded local bytes; ordered tree builder over strict sax.parser(true) events
scope: One namespace-aware XML 1.0 document from local bytes as an ordered xml-js tree; adapter expands qualified names using xmlns attributes
family: sax-js strict XML state machine (sax 1.6.1) under xml-js tree builder
family_note: xml-js 1.6.11 hardcodes pureJsParser=true and drives sax.parser(true, {}) for tokenization. It builds an ordered tree from SAX events and retains comments and processing instructions. Namespace expansion is performed by the adapter from preserved xmlns attributes. Shares the pinned sax 1.6.1 tokenizer with selected sax and xml2js paths.
verification_note: Docker valid-control replay matches the Expat oracle on both namespace-aware controls. V8 coverage counts 163 xml-js lib/xml2js.js tree-builder lines and 888 underlying sax lib/sax.js tokenizer lines separately. AFL++ feedback is scoped to the sax file only and is stable on repeated valid-control replays with an input-dependent 40-feature/40-tuple difference. xml-js delegates tokenization to the same sax 1.6.1 code selected independently as sax and by xml2js; it adds ordered tree construction, not an independent tokenizer. Namespace URI expansion is done by the adapter from preserved xmlns attributes. The hardcoded pureJsParser=true path does not use the optional node-expat import. Two valid controls do not prove complete XML conformance; no malformed, resource-use or campaign tests were run.
